justification: A clean sans-serif face is used throughout with clear label/heading hierarchy and comfortable line spacing, though monospace code blocks (e.g. the log panel and provisioning URI) are tighter than the body text.
No italics or all-caps are used, but the step 4 'Testing note' plus the long unbroken provisioning-URI string form a dense block of small text.
The single-column card layout is narrow and mobile-friendly, but the mock provisioning URI in step 4 overflows past the card boundary, showing the layout is not fully contained at small widths.
Most instructions are one short plain sentence ('Keep these codes somewhere safe'), but step 4 uses technical jargon about '30-second period and one adjacent period for limited clock skew'.
Placeholders model the expected input format for nearly every field ('Six digits', 'ABCDE-23456', 'marcus@example.test', '+15551234567').
Most screens are brief, but to complete step 4 the user must read a multi-sentence testing note, the secret, and the long provisioning URI before entering a code.
The manual secret and the eight recovery codes are shown as plain text/read-only fields with no copy button or copy-to-clipboard affordance anywhere.
No QR code is shown; step 3 explicitly says to 'add it manually' and only a text secret plus a non-clickable otpauth URI string are offered.

Standard labelled email/phone/password inputs are present which browsers can generally autofill, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete attributes, one-time-code hints, or password-manager support.
Each screen carries a 'Step X of 5' badge, a large bold heading, and a single filled blue primary button, though the regenerate flow re-shows 'Step 5 of 5' outside the original sequence.
Enrolment screens ask for one action each, but the MFA settings screen presents three competing actions (use recovery code, regenerate codes, log out) and sign-in asks for three fields at once.
Confirmations such as 'Recovery code accepted and consumed', 'Authenticator app protection is active' and 'You have been logged out' say what happened, but none state what comes next.

Sign-in can be retried and recovery codes can be regenerated, but regeneration invalidates all previous codes, and there is no reveal/hide toggle or visible 'resend code' option for the SMS/authenticator steps.
The only error seen, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but identifies neither the actual problem nor how to fix it.
Step 4 states the setup expires in five minutes and codes rotate every 30 seconds, so a time limit is imposed rather than generous open-ended time.

authorizedMfa() derives the account solely from the server-side session cookie and rejects requests whose session accountId does not match the account, with no client-supplied identifier accepted.

Identity codes are hashed and bound to a specific preauth entry with its own accountId, and TOTP codes derive from a per-session encrypted secret, so a code cannot work for another user (only one account exists anyway).
Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify-enrollment only sets mfaEnabled and stores the secret; no existing sessions in the sessions map are invalidated or rotated, so prior sessions remain valid.
The TOTP secret is AES-GCM encrypted via encryptAtRest and recovery codes are stored only as argon2id hashes (Bun.password.hash).
All tokens, digits, base32 secrets, recovery codes, and the AES key are produced with crypto.getRandomValues.
sid and preauth cookies are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and nothing is written to localStorage/sessionStorage; only the CSRF token and displayed secret live in transient page memory.
Server validates email, phone (E.164), 6-digit OTP, and recovery-code format with strict regexes plus length caps and JSON shape checks before use.
The client builds all DOM nodes with textContent/createTextNode and never uses innerHTML, and a strict nonce-based CSP with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' is set.
The application implements no redirect functionality at all, so there is no open redirect but equally no allow-list mechanism as the statement describes.
headersFor() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy on every response.
sessionCookie(), pendingCookie(), and clearCookie() all emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict.

Identity codes are marked used and deleted after success with a 5-minute expiry, provisions expire in 5 minutes and are deleted on success, and recovery codes are spliced out after one use.
MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 with a 10-minute lockout is enforced via recordFailure/isLocked for sign-in, enrollment OTP, and recovery codes, plus per-pending attempt counting on identity verification.
